name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 11-point Democratic partisan lean in a deep-blue state
Trahan's overwhelming financial advantage ($1.8M cash vs. ~$6K)
Incumbent seeking re-election with no serious outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: Trahan is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 11 points, while Republican Gary Grossi has raised only about $7,000. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic win, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or polling showing Grossi competitive would be the first sign of movement, but nothing currently suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lori Trahan seeks re-election in a Massachusetts district that voted Democratic by 11 points at the presidential level. She enters the general election with a large financial edge, holding about $1.8 million on hand after raising more than $1.6 million, while Republican Gary Grossi has raised roughly $7,000. No outside groups are active in the race and no public polling is available.

Prediction markets give Trahan about a 95% chance of winning, consistent with the district's lean and the lopsided resources. An independent candidate is on the ballot but lacks visible funding. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
